title: Flat fibre base change with compatible quasi-coherent coefficients
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a locally finite type morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $g:S'\to S$ any morphism, and $\mathcal F$ any quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Form $X'=X\times_SS'$ with projections $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to S'$ [def-pc-base-change], and put $\mathcal F'=(g')^*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let $r'\in S'$, $r=g(r')$, $k=\kappa(r)$, $k'=\kappa(r')$ [def-weil-residue-field], $Y=X_r$ and $Y'=X'_{r'}$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Write $i:Y\to X$, $i':Y'\to X'$ for the fibre projections and $\pi:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\pi':Y'\to\operatorname{Spec}k'$ for the structure maps [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then there is a canonical morphism $h:Y'\to Y$ with $i\circ h=g'\circ i'$ and $\pi\circ h=\operatorname{Spec}(k\to k')\circ\pi'$, making $Y'=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$. The morphism $h$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], $Y$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], $\mathcal F_r=i^*\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent, and there is a canonical isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{Y'}$-modules $\mathcal F'_{r'}=(i')^*\mathcal F'\cong h^*\mathcal F_r$.

source.place: Tag 05DC (lemma-base-change-relative-assassin), proof, first paragraph before the use of 05DB: fibre square, coefficient comparison, flatness, and locally Noetherian fibre.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-of-base-change] to $f,g,r\prime$. It gives the canonical $h:Y\prime\to Y$, both asserted projection equations, and the cartesian square over $\operatorname{Spec}(k\to k\prime)$. Thus $Y\prime=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k\prime$ with these projections.

source.place: Tag 05DC, lemma-base-change-relative-assassin, proof, first sentence and fibre-product display.

proof.text: The residue map $k\to k\prime$ is a field extension by [def-weil-residue-field]. Hence $a=\operatorname{Spec}(k\to k\prime):\operatorname{Spec}k\prime\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat by [lem-pc-field-extension-flat]. By step 1, $(Y\prime,\pi\prime,h)$ is a fibre product $\operatorname{Spec}k\prime\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}Y$ of $a$ and $\pi:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ (the cartesian square of step 1 with its two factors listed in the other order), and $h$ is its projection to $Y$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] to the flat morphism $a$ and the morphism $\pi$: the projection to $Y$, that is $h$, is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism].

source.place: Tag 01U9, lemma-base-change-flat; used in Tag 05DC (divisors.tex, lemma-base-change-relative-assassin), proof, first paragraph.

proof.text: The structure map $\pi:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change], applied to $f$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k\to S$. Every ideal of a field is either zero or the unit ideal, generated respectively by $0$ or $1$; thus $k$ is Noetherian. Its spectrum has the one-member affine cover with ring $k$, so is locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] to $\pi$ to obtain that $Y$ is locally Noetherian. Only local finite type is used; $Y$ need not be quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 05DC, proof, first paragraph; Morphisms Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian, locally Noetherian case.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent] to $i:Y\to X$ and the given quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$. Its conclusion is exactly that $\mathcal F_r=i^*\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent; no coherence or finite-generation assumption on $\mathcal F$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 01BG, lemma-pullback-quasi-coherent; used in Tag 05DC, first paragraph.

proof.text: Use the canonical tensor-pullback composition isomorphisms explicitly included in [def-pc-module-pullback]. The equation $g\prime\circ i\prime=i\circ h$ from step 1 gives the composite of canonical isomorphisms $$\mathcal F\prime_{r\prime}=(i\prime)^*(g\prime)^*\mathcal F\cong(g\prime\circ i\prime)^*\mathcal F=(i\circ h)^*\mathcal F\cong h^*i^*\mathcal F=h^*\mathcal F_r.$$ The first comparison is inverse composition and the second is forward composition, so this specifies a canonical $\mathcal O_{Y\prime}$-linear isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0097, lemma-push-pull-composition-modules, applied to the two composites; coefficient identification in Tag 05DC, proof, first paragraph.
